title: Chocolate Bomb
text: “Hey, Spear Hero. What exactly are you standing around gawking for? Leave that guy alone and eventually he’ll start researching how to make Filolials produce chocolate out of their rear ends! In the previous world the Shield Hero somehow managed to put a stop to it, but who knows what’ll happen in this world?”

What did you say!? Come to think of it, I believe Chick did mention something along those lines. Could it be that in previous loops as well, this same research had been conducted? Then this is absolutely unforgivable, I say!
“Chocolate from the rear end… well, in my world there are products themed after horse droppings, but they’re not literally made of the stuff… so this guy’s some kind of outrageous scat freak, huh.”

I recall Father calling a certain someone by that very name back in the first world. So it was him all along. But wait… I do recall that during the Chocolate Monster incident, the very chocolate this man made had ended up flowing into Zeltoble, and actually played a part in helping defeat the Chocolate Monster… Ha! Which means the chocolate that happens to be Ramfi’s weakness is right there!

“Spear Hero, let me guess what you’re thinking. You think this man’s chocolate will work on me, don’t you? Unfortunately, it has no effect on me now. But if you dare throw that chocolate at me, do you understand what will start coming out of my beloved Filo’s rear end instead?”
“Gah!”
Damn you, Ramfi! Surely you don’t mean to make chocolate come out of Filo-tan!?
“What kind of threat is that? It’s vulgar, please stop.”
“Now then, let’s be off.”
“No! Nooooo! Help meeeee! Boss! Weeeeerner!”
“The rest of you bandits, get thrown out already. Come on, you’re coming too!”
And with that, Ramfi dragged the bandit along, singling out the leader of Ren’s companions as well, and started walking.
“S-someone! Please stop this person! Otherwise this guy’s old man is in for something terrible!”
“If anything, I’d like to know how you’d even go about stopping this thing, Naofumi!”
Ren asked Father. I too would like to hear the means by which one might stop Ramfi, I say.
“I don’t know why you’re asking me, but is there anyone out there who can actually stop Ramfi-chan?”
I’m right here! Someday I will absolutely stop this thing and give Filo-tan a loving embrace, I say!
“Azott, are you coming too? The Shield Hero can’t cross the border, so if you’re going, go later.”
“N-no…”
“Hmph… fine, whatever. I’ll teach Luna and Keel to properly cherish chocolate later, then.”
“Why does it come to that!”
“The one here now is Yuki, is it… perfect timing. Yuki, let me teach you that chocolate is a gift that governs love. It’s especially effective when given to someone you have feelings for, you know?”
“I-is that true?”

Oh? Yuki-chan seems interested in giving chocolate to someone she has feelings for. Surely it must be chocolate meant for the Filolial-sama she was close with back in the first world? There’s no Filolial-sama faster on their feet than Yuki-chan around these days, but I suppose her interest lies in the act of giving, regardless.
“It seems there’s no stopping this. Motoyasu-sama, what will you do?”
“For the sake of Filolial-sama, I must go, I say.”
And so, for Filolial-sama’s sake, I ended up accompanying them. Father and Ren stayed behind to mind the fort.

And so we arrived at the Valentine’s Event region. It was an area where various chocolate trees were cultivated on what were called chocolate farms. I too had been around these parts before. Chocolate grew right there on the trees.
“Brings back memories. When things are peaceful, Azott often stays around here to help keep the peace.”
“Ren-sama did?”
Ren’s companion leader wore a dubious expression. No doubt questioning why that Ren would have frequented his own hometown.
“Yeah. That’s Azott for you. I never heard it from him directly, but perhaps he was making amends, thinking of you who died partway through your ambitions.”

Now that I think of it, Ren’s companions in the first world apparently were all wiped out. Perhaps he knew something about that. But by that same logic, I recall hearing that Ren had stayed in several other regions together with Éclair and Assistant as well. Could it be… that his other companions also hail from unusual regions? Given that back in the game era there were all sorts of seasonal events—New Year’s, Christmas, Halloween—that might well be the case.

Ren’s companion leader fell into a complicated silence. According to Father from some world or other, Ren is the type to quietly do good deeds that slowly grow on you once you learn of them—the sort that makes you come to like him. Well, Ren isn’t the type to volunteer the reason behind his peacekeeping himself. If he went around bragging about that kind of thing, it wouldn’t really count as making amends in the first place. Still, I feel like the Ren from worlds with no connection to these people came around here too…
“Mmf! Mmmmf!”

Meanwhile, the bandit, bound up and gagged, was being carried along. Ramfi seemed to have a good sense of the local geography, marching straight to the bandit’s family home without so much as a word to the farmers along the way. Erasing all presence, she peeked into an odd structure behind the house, confirmed someone was inside, and called us over. Then, out of nowhere, Ramfi casually pulled out what looked like a grenade-shaped explosive.
“Watch closely. And take joy in watching your father suffer. The fool who turned chocolate into a tool for boasting, a mere plaything! Take this! Pineapple Chocolate Bomb!”

With a click, she pulled the pin and tossed the grenade into the building—and with a resounding splat, a huge noise rang out. I could almost hear Father from the first world demanding, “Who on earth made that thing?”
“Gyaaaaaaaaah!? Wh-what!? Has someone come to silence me after stealing my research!?”
The man came tumbling out, utterly covered in chocolate. Was this the bandit’s father, then? An enemy of Filolial-sama! Shall I pursue with a Paralyze Lance?
“Hmph! I’ve come to put an end to your ridiculous inventions—your acts of blasphemy!”
Ramfi shifted her shape and bound him up like a chocolate egg, leaving only his face exposed. I could almost hear Father from the first world scoffing and saying, “Ha! What a pathetic chocolate egg!”
“How dare you call my inventions ridiculous! My love is absolute! Someday my inventions will resound across the world, and everyone will crave my chocolate!”

“Hmph. Still spouting the same nonsense as always, I see. You were like this in every world. Just when I think you might have reflected a little, a few years pass and, without learning a thing, you start churning out more worthless, trite garbage. It was the same back then too.”
“Who do you think you are! You insolent brat!”
“Oh my, how cold. I’ve known you since you were small, you know?”
Fufu—Ramfi spoke to the hardened bandit father with a confident smirk.

“While your parent was alive, you couldn’t defy them, diligently tending to the chocolate trees, offering up the fruits of your labor to me with a smile. Well… you did make things of reasonable quality, and were recognized by those around you. If only you’d kept living steadily like that… but the moment your parent was gone, this is what happened.”

They seemed to share quite a familiar relationship. Well, I suppose Ramfi is apparently the origin of the Chocolate Monster after all. …Does she feel nothing about having been modified by Ren? This thing exists by some standard that’s utterly beyond me, I say.
“Shut up, shut up! Finally that old relic clinging to outdated methods, wielding nothing but authority, is gone! I, the pioneer of a new era, shall birth new chocolate!”
“Ra-ra-ra… you think of yourself as young? Now that’s hilarious.”
Well, he certainly wasn’t young, that much was true.
“Or are you speaking of your spirit? That would make sense. Truly childish! Now that I think of it, your fondest memory was winning some award at age eight, wasn’t it? Ra-ra-ra.”
“Whaaaaaaaat!?”
Just as Father from the first world once said—this was one loud old man. I understood exactly why Father found him so exasperating.
